p: these are the seven mitzvos of the festival,
the four species of the lulav,
If there is simchah, why chagigah?
And if there is chagigah, why simchah?"
The commentators explained that this is a question left without an answer,
and simchah as the shelamim of simchah.
But in truth it is possible
that the Midrash explains the seven joys
for regarding the four species it is written (Vayikra 23:40):
"And you shall rejoice before Hashem your God," etc.
in the sense of what Tosafos wrote
some explain it as a term of dancing,
כְּמוֹ יָחוֹגּוּ וְיָנוּעוּ כַּשִּׁכּוֹר (תְּהִלִּים קז, כז).
as in 'They reel and stagger like a drunkard'" (Tehillim 107:27).
That is, when one nullifies himself
for the honor of Hashem, blessed be He,
"And David danced with all his might
לִפְנֵי ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר (שְׁמוּאֵל ב ו, יד),
"As one of the empty fellows shamelessly uncovers himself," etc. (ibid. 20).
That is, he nullified his entire mind
for the honor of Hashem, blessed be He.
And similar to what we find (Kesubos 17a):
would dance juggling three myrtle branches.
"The old man is embarrassing us," etc.;
"it was of benefit to him," etc.,
for he behaved like a fool
for the sake of Heaven, for the sake of a mitzvah.
And on this Tosafos brings the comparison
"as in 'They reel and stagger like a drunkard,'"
for he nullifies his entire mind for the sake of Heaven.
"You shall make for yourself the festival of Sukkos
seven days, when you gather in," etc.;
and it is written (ibid. 14): "And you shall rejoice in your festival" —
this refers to both of them:
and to the mitzvah of chag,
when there is no mitzvah at all,
only the fixing of the joy,
so that it should have lasting existence for all eternity.
correspond to the seven shepherds, the Ushpizin:
שֶׁאַרְבָּעָה מִינִים נִדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל, י)
for the four species are expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 30:10)
as corresponding to the Avos and Yosef:
פְּרִי עֵץ הָדָר זֶה אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵּי,
"'The fruit of a beautiful tree' — this is Avraham, etc.;
'branches of date palms' — this is Yitzchak, etc.;
וַעֲנַף עֵץ עָבוֹת זֶה יַעֲקֹב וְכוּלֵּי,
'and the bough of a thick-leaved tree' — this is Yaakov, etc.;
'and willows of the brook' — this is Yosef," etc.
And simchah corresponds to Moshe Rabbeinu,
as we say (in the Shabbos morning prayer):
"Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion" —
which was given to him as a gift.
for we rejoice without any mitzvah,
"The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart";
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סוֹף פֶּרֶק א דְּתַעֲנִית, טו, א).
(as stated at the end of the first perek of Taanis, 15a).
in whose merit they merited the Clouds of Glory
וַחֲגִיגָה נֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And chagigah corresponds to David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
in whom we find the dancing and leaping,
for he nullified himself and his own honor
for the honor of Hashem, blessed be He,
and I will be held even more lightly than this," etc.
the expression "They reel and stagger like a drunkard."
And on Shabbos all of Yisrael merit
for Shabbos — since according to all opinions
the Torah was given on Shabbos
"Malchus is the mouth, the Torah she'b'al peh"
And this is what we say (in the Shabbos prayers):
"Those who keep Shabbos shall rejoice in Your kingship."
